candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Safe Use of Equipment / client safety activities, printed pp.24-26
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — procedural safety and safe technology use
candidate.educational_objective: When adjunct technology is part of the facility RSI-prevention process, complete it before wound closure even when the manual count is correct.

options.A: Allow closure because a correct manual count makes RF verification unnecessary
options.B: Complete the required RF verification before final wound closure and communicate any discrepancy
options.C: Skip RF verification if the scrub person and surgeon verbally confirm the count
options.D: Allow closure and perform RF verification after the client leaves the OR

candidate.rationale: Manual counts can be falsely reassuring. AORN recommends adjunct technology as a supplement when used and directs completion of the manual count and adjunct verification before wound closure according to manufacturer instructions and facility policy. Verbal agreement does not replace the established verification process, and post-closure verification is too late for its prevention purpose.
candidate.source_claim_supported: AORN supports adjunct technology as a supplement to manual counting and states to complete both before wound closure when adjunct technology is used.
candidate.source_document_title: Using Adjunct Technology with the Surgical Count
candidate.source_locator: Considerations for Using Adjunct Technology — follow IFU/facility policy; use adjunct technology even when manual count is correct; complete manual count and adjunct technology before wound closure
candidate.stem: A facility uses RF adjunct technology plus manual sponge counts. At the end of an abdominal procedure, the manual closing count is correct but RF verification is not yet done. The surgeon asks to complete wound closure. What should the circulating nurse do?
